items.correct: Stable internal conditions within narrow limits, despite external change.
items.misconception: Conditions that never vary at all.
items.random_wrong: Only the body's temperature, nothing else.
items.why: Negative feedback keeps factors like temperature, water and glucose around a set point.

items.q: What does insulin do to blood glucose?
items.correct: Lowers it, by making cells take up glucose.
items.why: Insulin lowers blood glucose; glucagon raises it — they act antagonistically.

items.q: How does sweating affect body temperature?
items.correct: It cools you as the sweat evaporates.
items.random_wrong: It has no effect on temperature.
items.why: Evaporating sweat removes heat (cooling); shivering generates heat (warming).
